answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before its votes or reputation count. A newcomer’s influence then grows only as the identity completes costly, independently checked tasks; copying a profile creates no extra stake or history. This makes a sybil swarm expensive: the attacker must buy and immobilize tokens for every account, while one detected fake can trigger a ripple that removes its thread of linked rewards. A hollow identity earns nothing until it pays the same entry cost.
